plan: OpenVibe.Food starts from the OpenVibe service skeleton; the product's own plan is written here when it is
summary: OpenVibe.Food — What should we eat? A new OpenVibe service on the shared skeleton, not deployed yet: sign-in with OpenVibe.Network (OAuth 2 + PKCE, httpOnly session cookies), server-rendered pages through the OpenVibe Frame, the /api/v1 mount with per-caller limits, crawl artifacts, PostgreSQL migrations applied at boot, the nginx and systemd deploy files and a test suite on PGlite with a mock Network.
works: Sign-in with OpenVibe.Network (PKCE S256, server-side code exchange, httpOnly session cookies)
Server-rendered pages: the home page and /updates, through the OpenVibe Frame, complete without JavaScript
Crawl artifacts: robots.txt, sitemap.xml, llms.txt, llms-full.txt and the home page's JSON-LD
The API mount at /api/v1 with the problem+json error shape, the per-address limits and the per-caller limits
Capability verification for app, agent and service tokens (audience openvibe.food) and for a person's own token
Truthful readiness (/api/ready: the database is required) and Prometheus metrics on loopback
PostgreSQL with migrations/NNNN_*.sql (openvibe-sdk/db); PGlite in development
Tests on a temp PGlite database with an in-process mock of OpenVibe.Network
notYet: The product itself: its tables and migrations, its capabilities, its routes in server/http/api.js and its pages in server/http/pages.js
Its service and capability manifests in openvibe-contracts (contracts-service is food)
A deployment: the service is not registered with OpenVibe.Services nor deployed by OpenVibe.Host
